areas.n: Chiyoda-ku (Imperial Palace · Marunouchi · Akihabara · Kanda · Jimbōchō)

P.n: Imperial Palace East Gardens (皇居東御苑)
P.w: The free public garden on the old honmaru of Edo Castle — the castle-keep base, guardhouses and a seasonal garden inside the palace walls.
The 1869 Shintō shrine to Japan's war dead — great torii, cherry-tree avenue and the Yūshūkan war museum; politically contested, historically essential.
1,300-year-old shrine of Edo's merchants, home of the Kanda Matsuri — and, a block from Akihabara, an anime pilgrimage stop (Love Live!) with IT-blessing omamori.

P.n: Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building (東京駅丸の内駅舎)
P.w: Tatsuno Kingo's 1914 red-brick station front, restored with its twin domes in 2012 — a nationally Important Cultural Property.

P.n: National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo (MOMAT)
P.w: Japan's first national art museum — the definitive collection of 20th-century Japanese painting (Kishida, Yokoyama Taikan) beside the palace moat.

P.n: Akihabara Electric Town (秋葉原電気街)
P.w: Tokyo's electronics-and-otaku quarter — multi-storey arcades, figure shops, retro-game dens and maid cafés around Chūō-dōri.

P.n: Jimbōchō Book Town (神保町古書店街)
P.w: 100+ second-hand and antiquarian bookshops along Yasukuni-dōri — named Time Out's World's Coolest Neighbourhood 2025; also a curry-rice heartland.
Hilltop shrine of the Sannō Matsuri, reached by an escalator or a tunnel of vermilion torii on its west stair.
The octagonal 1964 Olympic judo hall that became Japan's rock temple (the Beatles, 1966) — still the martial-arts and concert landmark of Kitanomaru Park.
Tokyo's oldest temple (founded 645) — through the Kaminarimon thunder gate and the Nakamise-dōri stall street to the main hall and five-storey pagoda.

P.n: Tokyo National Museum (東京国立博物館)
P.w: Japan's oldest and largest museum — 120,000 objects including 89 National Treasures, from Jōmon pottery to samurai armour and ukiyo-e, in Ueno Park.
Japan's first public park (1873) — museums, the zoo, Shinobazu Pond's lotus beds, Tōshō-gū and Tokyo's most famous cherry-blossom avenue. Free entry.
'Kitchen Town' — some 170 shops between Ueno and Asakusa selling knives, lacquerware, noren and the plastic food samples of every Japanese shop window.
The national sumo hall — three of the six annual grand tournaments (January, May, September) are fought here; the Sumo Museum and the chanko-nabe restaurants of Ryōgoku surround it.

P.n: Sumida Hokusai Museum (すみだ北斎美術館)
P.w: Kazuyo Sejima's faceted aluminium museum (2016) for Hokusai, who spent most of his 88 years in Sumida — his life, his prints and the neighbourhood that shaped them.
Meiji-era stroll garden built by the Iwasaki (Mitsubishi) family — a big pond, stepping stones of prized rock from across Japan, carp, turtles and a lakeside teahouse.
Edo-period shrine in old-town Yanesen with a tunnel of small vermilion torii and a hillside of some 3,000 azaleas each April.

P.n: Shibuya Scramble Crossing (渋谷スクランブル交差点)
P.w: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing — up to 3,000 people per green light outside Shibuya Station and the Hachikō statue; watch it from Shibuya Sky or the station's upper floors.
Big, informal park beside Meiji Jingū — weekend buskers, rockabilly dancers, ginkgo avenues in autumn and festivals on the event plaza.

P.n: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (新宿御苑)
P.w: Former imperial garden blending French formal, English landscape and Japanese styles — 1,000 cherry trees, a tropical greenhouse and a teahouse, minutes from Shinjuku Station.

P.n: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (東京都庁)
P.w: Kenzo Tange's twin-towered city hall with free 202 m observation decks — Mt Fuji on clear winter mornings and an evening projection-mapping show on the facade.

P.n: Shinjuku Golden Gai (新宿ゴールデン街)
P.w: Six narrow lanes of 200-odd postwar shoebox bars, each seating a handful — the most atmospheric drinking quarter in Tokyo.
Shrine to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken in a 70-hectare planted forest between Harajuku and Yoyogi — giant cypress torii, sake-barrel wall, and Japan's busiest New Year hatsumōde.

P.n: Tokyo Skytree (東京スカイツリー)
P.w: At 634 m the world's tallest tower — observation decks at 350 m and 450 m, with Tokyo Solamachi mall and an aquarium at its foot.
Yanagisawa Yoshiyasu's 1702 stroll garden recreating 88 scenes from waka poetry — a weeping cherry in spring and lantern-lit maples in autumn.
Tokyo's oldest daimyō garden (1629, Mito Tokugawa) — the Engetsu-kyō full-moon bridge, plum grove and miniature Chinese and Japanese landscapes beside Tokyo Dome.
Tokyo's grand kabuki theatre behind a Momoyama-style facade — buy a single-act makumi ticket on the day to sample a play from the top gallery.
The 1911 granite bridge at 'kilometre zero' of Japan's roads — the start of the Edo-period Tōkaidō, bronze kirin on its lamps, the expressway overhead soon to be buried.
Shōgun's former duck-hunting garden on Tokyo Bay with a tidal seawater pond and the Nakajima teahouse for matcha, ringed by Shiodome towers.
The Tokugawa shōguns' family temple — the 1622 Sangedatsumon gate, rows of jizō statues in knitted caps, and Tokyo Tower rising directly behind the main hall.

P.n: Roppongi Hills Mori Tower — Tokyo City View & Mori Art Museum
P.w: The 54-storey heart of Roppongi Hills: the Mori Art Museum's contemporary shows and the Tokyo City View deck on the 52nd floor.
P.k: Mori Art Museum, Tokyo City View

P.w: Barefoot immersive digital-art museum in Toyosu — wade knee-deep through projected koi, a floating-flower dome and a mirrored infinity crystal universe.
Tokyo's wholesale fish market since 2018 — watch the dawn tuna auction from the observation gallery, then sushi breakfast in the market restaurants.
Fukagawa's great Hachiman shrine — birthplace of Edo kanjin sumo (the yokozuna monument stands here) and host of the water-splashing Fukagawa Hachiman festival.
Japan's major public contemporary-art museum, in Kiba Park near Kiyosumi-Shirakawa's coffee roasters.

P.n: Nakano Broadway (中野ブロードウェイ)
P.w: 1966 shopping-and-apartment complex turned otaku mecca — four floors of Mandarake, vintage toys, manga, idol goods and watch dealers at the end of Nakano Sun Mall.
Tokyo's bohemian village of vintage-clothing shops, tiny theatres, live houses and coffee stands around Shimo-kitazawa Station and the Ichibangai shopping street.
The 333 m orange-and-white 1958 lattice tower — Main Deck at 150 m and Top Deck at 250 m, and still the city's favourite night-skyline icon.
Small Takanawa temple holding the graves of the 47 rōnin of Akō — incense is still lit at each grave, and a festival marks their vendetta every 14 December.

P.n: Ghibli Museum, Mitaka (三鷹の森ジブリ美術館)
P.w: Hayao Miyazaki's own whimsical museum on the edge of Inokashira Park — animation workshops, a Catbus room, a rooftop Laputa robot and short films shown only here. Advance tickets only.
Kichijōji's beloved park — swan boats on a cherry-lined pond, the Benzaiten shrine and weekend craft stalls, a short walk from the Ghibli Museum.
599 m sacred mountain an hour from Shinjuku — cable car or trails up to Yakuō-in temple and a summit view of Mt Fuji on clear days.
Tokyo's second-oldest temple (733) in a spring-fed forest, ringed by soba shops making Jindai-ji soba from the local water.

P.n: Great Buddha of Kamakura — Kōtoku-in (鎌倉大仏)
P.w: The 13.35 m bronze Amida Buddha (1252) sitting in the open air since a 15th-century tsunami washed its hall away — you can step inside the hollow statue.
Kamakura's central shrine, founded by Minamoto no Yoritomo — a grand approach from the sea up Dankazura, lotus ponds and a hilltop main hall.
Tokugawa Ieyasu's lavishly carved mausoleum shrine in cedar forest — the Yōmeimon gate, the three wise monkeys and the sleeping cat; part of the UNESCO Shrines and Temples of Nikkō.
Daikyō-ji, the shitamachi temple of the 'Tora-san' films — its halls wrapped in astonishing wood-carved panels, reached down the Taishakuten-sandō street of kusa-dango and senbei shops.

P.n: Kasai Rinkai Park (葛西臨海公園)
P.w: Bayside park with a giant Ferris wheel, a bird sanctuary, a beach and the Tokyo Sea Life Park aquarium's tuna doughnut tank.

P.n: Holy Resurrection Cathedral — Nikolai-dō (ニコライ堂)
P.w: Green-domed 1891 Byzantine-style Orthodox cathedral founded by St Nicholas of Japan, rising unexpectedly over Ochanomizu.

P.n: Tokyo International Forum (東京国際フォーラム)
P.w: Rafael Viñoly's 1996 glass-hull atrium between Yūrakuchō and Tokyo Station — free to walk through, with a weekend antique market on the plaza.

P.n: Shibuya Sky — Shibuya Scramble Square (渋谷スカイ)
P.w: Open-air rooftop deck 230 m above the Scramble Crossing on top of the 2019 Shibuya Scramble Square tower — sunset over Mt Fuji is the prize.
Bronze of the Akita who waited at Shibuya Station for his dead master for nearly ten years — Tokyo's most famous meeting point.

P.n: Yebisu Garden Place (恵比寿ガーデンプレイス)
P.w: Plaza on the site of the old Yebisu brewery — the beer's birthplace brewery restarted here, plus the Tokyo Photographic Art Museum and a Baccarat chandelier each winter.
Tadao Ando's spiral-ramp mall on the zelkova-lined Omotesandō boulevard — the avenue of architect-designed flagships between Harajuku and Aoyama.
Kengo Kuma's bamboo-lined museum of pre-modern Asian art (Kōrin's Irises screen each spring) with a deep, hilly stroll garden and teahouses behind.

P.n: The National Art Center, Tokyo (国立新美術館)
P.w: Kisho Kurokawa's undulating glass-facade exhibition hall in Roppongi — Japan's largest exhibition space, no permanent collection, a cone-top café.

P.n: Kyū-Shiba-rikyū Gardens (旧芝離宮恩賜庭園)
P.w: One of Tokyo's oldest daimyō stroll gardens (1678), a pond landscape tucked beside Hamamatsuchō Station.

P.n: Rainbow Bridge (レインボーブリッジ)
P.w: Suspension bridge to Odaiba with a free pedestrian promenade on each side — the classic view back to the Tokyo skyline and Tokyo Tower, lit at night.

P.n: National Museum of Western Art (国立西洋美術館)
P.w: Le Corbusier's only building in East Asia — part of the UNESCO Le Corbusier serial site — housing the Matsukata collection of Rodin, Monet and Old Masters; Rodin's Gates of Hell stand in the forecourt.
Josiah Conder's 1896 Jacobean-style mansion for the Mitsubishi Iwasaki family, with a Japanese wing and a Swiss-chalet billiard house — Meiji Westernisation in one garden.
Leafy old cemetery of shōguns' retainers and Meiji notables — cherry-tree avenues, the last shōgun Tokugawa Yoshinobu's tomb and the neighbourhood's resident cats.
The 1649 Gongen-style shrine beside Sensō-ji honouring the temple's three founders, home of the riotous Sanja Matsuri each May.
Josiah Conder's stone Western villa above a terraced rose garden that steps down to a Japanese pond garden by Ogawa Jihei — spectacular at the May and October rose festivals.

P.n: Sunshine City, Ikebukuro (サンシャインシティ)
P.w: Ikebukuro's mega-complex — the rooftop Sunshine Aquarium with its 'sky penguins', Namjatown, the Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo and the Sunshine 60 observatory — next to Otome Road.

P.n: Jiyū Gakuen Myōnichikan (自由学園明日館)
P.w: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1921 Prairie-style school building with Arata Endo — an Important Cultural Property where you can take tea in the double-height hall.

P.n: Meguro Parasitological Museum (目黒寄生虫館)
P.w: Free, gloriously odd private museum of some 300 parasite specimens — the star is an 8.8 m tapeworm.

P.n: Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Art Museum (東京都庭園美術館)
P.w: Prince Asaka's 1933 Art Deco residence — Lalique glass doors, Henri Rapin interiors — used as an exhibition museum inside a Japanese and Western garden.
The 'cat temple' said to be the birthplace of the maneki-neko — thousands of white beckoning cats lined up beside the hall, under a 22.5 m three-tiered pagoda.
Hilltop head temple of Nichiren Buddhism on the site where Nichiren died in 1282 — with the oldest five-storey pagoda in the Kantō region.

F.n: Chukasoba Ginza Hachigou (銀座 八五)
F.w: A tiny Ginza counter where a French-trained chef builds a clear, consommé-like shōyu chūka soba — Tokyo-style ramen at its most refined.
Roppongi branch of the Michelin-listed Iruca — a delicate shōyu ramen finished with a fragrant porcini oil.
Shinjuku-gyoemmae ramen counter (once Michelin-starred) famous for a hamaguri-clam and pork broth shio soba lifted with truffle and porcini.
Neighbourhood soba-ya in Shimo-Ochiai listed by Michelin for hand-made seiro soba.
Nishi-Azabu soba house in the Michelin selection — hand-made soba and seasonal sake-side dishes.

F.n: Sosakumenkobo Nakiryu (創作麺工房 鳴龍)
F.w: Ōtsuka counter that held a Michelin star for its Sichuan-inspired tantanmen; still Michelin-listed and still queued for.
The cult tonkatsu that made pale, rosy low-temperature frying famous — Michelin-listed, long queues.
Yotsuya-area tonkatsu counter, a Michelin Bib Gourmand for its carefully fried branded-pork rosu and hire.

F.n: Tonkatsu Hinata (とんかつ ひなた)
F.w: Takadanobaba tonkatsu shop on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list — juicy, lightly-crumbed hire and rosu.
Ikegami neighbourhood tonkatsu near Honmon-ji, a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.n: Mochibuta Tonkatsu Taiyo (もち豚とんかつ たいよう)
F.w: Musashi-Koyama tonkatsu built on 'mochibuta' pork, a Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Ueno tonkatsu house in the Michelin Bib Gourmand selection.
Ikejiri-Ōhashi ramen shop whose silky shrimp-and-pork wonton-men in a white or black shōyu broth draws daily queues; Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.n: Ramenya Toy Box (らぁ麺屋 トイボックス)
F.w: Mikawashima/Nippori ramen-ya on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list for its clean chicken-based shio and shōyu bowls.

F.n: Homemade Ramen Muginae (自家製麺 麦苗)
F.w: Ōmori ramen shop making its own noodles daily — a Michelin Bib Gourmand and a ramen-otaku pilgrimage.

F.n: Ginza Haru Chan Ramen (銀座 春ちゃんラーメン)
F.w: Back-street Ginza ramen counter whose shio ramen won a Michelin Bib Gourmand in the 2026 guide — an affordable bowl a block from the luxury flagships.
Takaido shop devoted to shio (salt) soba, a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.n: Ramen Matsui (らぁ麺 まつい)
F.w: Yotsuya-sanchōme ramen shop with a Michelin Bib Gourmand in the 2026 guide.
Zaiyu Hasegawa's playful modern kaiseki — the famous 'Dentucky' chicken wing and a warmth that made it one of Tokyo's best-loved tables.
Yoshihiro Narisawa's 'innovative satoyama' cuisine — forest, sea and soil of Japan on the plate, opening with bread that rises and bakes at the table.

F.ad: 2F Azabudai Hills Garden Plaza D, 5-10-7 Toranomon, Minato-ku, Tokyo 105-0001
F.w: Hiroyasu Kawate's counter-theatre French tasting menu, relocated to Azabudai Hills.
Fumio Kondo's Ginza counter, the master of vegetable tempura — the slow-fried sweet potato is the signature.
Masahiro Yoshitake's top-tier Ginza Edomae sushi counter.

F.n: Kagurazaka Ishikawa (神楽坂 石かわ)
F.w: Hideki Ishikawa's kaiseki house tucked in a Kagurazaka back alley — the benchmark of Tokyo seasonal cooking.

F.n: Nodaiwa Azabu Iikura Honten (野田岩 麻布飯倉本店)
F.w: Fifth-generation unagi house in an old kura-style building near Tokyo Tower — wild-eel kabayaki in the Edo manner.

F.n: Onigiri Asakusa Yadoroku (おにぎり浅草宿六)
F.w: Tokyo's oldest onigiri shop (1954) — rice balls pressed to order at a tiny counter behind Sensō-ji; a Michelin Bib Gourmand and a dawn-queue favourite.
Yoshinori Watanabe's riverside French dining room in Komagata, Asakusa — Michelin one-star cooking looking across the Sumida to Skytree.
Noboru Arai's French restaurant in the back streets of Kannon-ura, Asakusa — two Michelin stars in the 2026 guide.
Small soba-ya near Kappabashi, a Michelin Bib Gourmand in the 2026 guide.
Michelin-listed Japanese counter in Kannon-ura, north of Sensō-ji.
Michelin-listed neighbourhood shokudō in Asakusa serving Japanese home-style set meals.

F.n: Myojinshita Soba Oshin (明神下 そば 押し)
F.w: Soba-ya just below Kanda Myōjin, in the 2026 Michelin selection — Kanda's soba tradition in a new generation.
Okachimachi yōshoku house (1905) credited with Tokyo's tonkatsu lineage — lard-fried katsuretsu; a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.n: Yaesu Unagi Hashimoto (八重洲 鰻 はし本)
F.w: Unagi specialist by Tokyo Station's Yaesu side, a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.n: Japanese Ramen Gokan (Japanese Ramen 五感)
F.w: Ikebukuro ramen shop with a Michelin Bib Gourmand in the 2026 guide.

F.ad: 1F Toranomon Hills Residential Tower, 1-1-1 Atago, Minato-ku, Tokyo 105-0002
F.w: Hiroyuki Kanda's eight-seat counter — three Michelin stars every year since the first Tokyo guide, now in Toranomon Hills.
Minami-Aoyama contemporary French in the Michelin selection — a relaxed, good-value tasting menu.
Asakusa Edomae sushi counter in the Michelin selection.
Shibuya basement shokudō built around bonito flakes shaved to order over rice and miso soup; Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026.

F.n: Ginza Katsukami II (銀座かつかみ II)
F.w: Ginza tonkatsu counter serving a prix-fixe of rare cuts — new Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026.
Yakitori bar run by two brothers in Higashi-Mukōjima, skewers mostly served salted — new Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026.
Shirokane yōshoku house with nostalgic hamburg steak in demi-glace — new Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026.

F.ad: 7F Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Marunouchi, 1-11-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 100-6277
F.w: Daniel Calvert's dining room above Tokyo Station — awarded three Michelin stars in the 18th Tokyo guide, French technique with Japanese ingredients.
Meguro-station yakitori counter on the Michelin Bib Gourmand list.

F.n: Jimbocho Gokita (神保町 五木田)
F.w: Jimbōchō 'neo-yakitori' — skewers paired with French sauces; Michelin-listed 2026.

F.n: Bird Land Ginza (バードランド 銀座)
F.w: Toshihiro Wada's basement yakitori under Ginza 4-chōme — the restaurant that took yakitori into the Michelin guide.
Oshiage yakitori counter in the shadow of Skytree, listed in the Michelin guide.
Kagurazaka-side yakitori bar, Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026.

F.n: Asagaya Bird Land (阿佐ヶ谷 バードランド)
F.w: The Asagaya original of the Bird Land yakitori family, in the Michelin selection.
Ginza Japanese restaurant newly awarded one Michelin star.
Shirokanedai basement tempura counter, one Michelin star in the 2026 guide.
Kagurazaka tempura counter in the Michelin selection.
Toru Okuda's Ginza kaiseki house — two Michelin stars in the 2026 guide.
Azabu-Jūban unagi specialist in the Michelin selection.

F.n: Sobakappo Nagano (蕎麦割烹 長野)
F.w: Higashi-Mukōjima soba-kappō — soba plus platters of small dishes made for sake; new Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026.

F.n: Tempura Abe Honten (天ぷら あべ 本店)
F.w: Ginza tempura shop in the Michelin selection with affordable lunch tempura (¥1,500–9,000).
Yoshinaga Jinbo's modern Italian that 'paints scenes of the fields on the plate' — Michelin-listed.
Gaienmae basement Japanese where char-grilled fish and rice cooked in an iron pot are the mainstays — Michelin-listed.
